source: I finally have the proof I need.
It's all contained within these pages, Mother.
For the rest of you: In summary, for all her faith, my mother is not faithful.
She gave her body to Claudius while my father was still living!
No! That's not...
Hamlet. Stop. Now.
Not only that, but Claudius had some hand in my father's death.
No. Not his death. His murder.
Hamlet, you're making no sense, my love. Please, stop!
You mean you had no idea anyone would find out. That's what this was about, isn't it? Keeping it hidden from me?
My father's death was no accident. You two planned to kill him. Admit it!
I beg you, stop this now!
Is something wrong?
You've got to come quickly.
I believe the Queen is a danger to herself at the moment. She needs you.
She's in the graveyard.
Take me to her.
Gerta. Look at me.
I can't.
She's been like this, mute, since... well.
Hamlet is... dead.
Hamlet brought this diary before us all. It spoke of the Queen's private life, and it was not kind.
The King cut him down. It was like nothing I've ever seen. Ophelia, it was horrifying.
(I brought that on Gertrude. On Hamlet. Oh, my God. He's dead?)
That play Hamlet put on. It spoke of the Queen's private life, and it was cruel.
The King cut him down. It was like nothing I've ever seen.
The going word is he threw himself from the walls. The Queen tried to stop him, but was unsuccessful.
Claudius had berated him cruelly for what he perceived to be rumormongering. Hamlet wasn't in his right mind.
She won't speak to anyone.
I can imagine not. She's just lost her son.
Is that Ophelia?
He's dead. My little boy is dead.
And he died hating me. I saw his face.
How can that be possible? How can the little boy I poured my heart into want to hurt me so much?
They bore him barefaced on the bier.
And in his grave rained many a tear.
I'm so sorry, my lady. This is all my fault.
It cannot be your fault, my sweet. I had hoped you would be my daughter in marriage someday.
Now that day will never come to pass.
My lady, we shall all reunite with our departed loved souls in Heaven above. Until then, we shall pray for the boy he was.
Aye. My Prince—he may have been led astray in the end, but we will remember him as he was before.
It had to be done. I killed him for you. Why did you run from me?
I berated the boy, but he did the deed himself. His mind was broken. I was merely the last straw on his back.
Why must you blame me?
O-Ophelia, please don't let him near me...
Not another step, Claudius.
You are my wife. I made a vow to protect you. And I'll uphold that vow, no matter what.
Hail, Claudius.
Hail the brother you killed.
My God—
What is that?
T-the spirit...?
You cannot escape the eye of Heaven, brother.
I came not to bring peace, but to bring a sword.
And now you have murdered my son. My only child. My greatest treasure.
This is madness!
This isn't...
I put you in the grave once, and I'll damn well do it again!
Grrrahh! Die!
Look upon me. Did Christ not say, 'Surely I am with you always'? As am I with you... my black touch descends on your sullied court...
Why are you doing this?
How strange and peculiar that you and I should meet now, at the end of time, at the end of this world.
Find me on the first night. You are too late for this fragment to exist. It will soon melt.
Die, damn you! Die! Die! Die!
The Ghost has made itself known.

source: I thought, last time...
(The ghost didn't appear.)
Don't you dare touch her, Claudius.
Shut the hell up. She's my wife. I'll do as I please.
Get up. Now. Stop making a scene.
Ahh—what have you done?
Throw me in jail if you like, my lady. Or have me hanged. Or worse.
I could not bear to watch him take another step.
Not after...
No. It is done.
Thank you, Horatio.
...We must bury the dead.
I've let everyone down. Absolutely everyone.
I cannot live for this, Lord. I'm sorry. I cannot obey your law.
Even though I know it is the gravest sin.
Every minute I spend forcing a smile, feeling like I want to die—
I feel such a weight upon me.
And Margaret has already gone to your side, Lord.
It seems so unfair that she should be in Heaven, and I here.
I long to hold her hand. To have just one conversation with her. To embrace her.
Hamlet, if you can hear my prayers, help me!
Everything we worked so hard to build has crumbled without your presence.
Our son, our kingdom, your legacy. I tried to keep it all together. But it was like sand slipping through my fingers.
Hamlet, my love, my husband.
Can you see the hell I'm in?
Speak to me, please, if you're there!
My lady.
Oh. Ophelia.
Don't do this.
Please. Come with me. Come off the ledge.
We still need you. I need you.
Ophelia. You must keep her safe.
After he died, I thought I could go on. I thought I would recover.
But I haven't. And my head-- is screaming at me that the world would be better off without me.
That I wouldn't make everyone else around me miserable anymore, that they could all move on and find happiness if I were just gone.
I know it feels that way, my lady. But it isn't true. It's only the voices in your head.
Come no closer. Stay, my sweet. Stay in the world of the living.
Ophelia, plead some sense with her!
My lady, let's go somewhere warmer and talk a while. I want to help you.
But first, you must come down from that ledge. Take my hand.
No! No, my mind is made, my purpose clear.
Margaret, perhaps God will pity me and let me join you still.
Here will I set up my everlasting rest...
And shake the yoke of inauspicious stars from this world-wearied flesh.
I brought this on her.
This is but one fragment.
A thousand times I've seen her die. Not once has it been less easy to bear.
You must save her, Ophelia. Save her from her pain.
But I haven't. And my head is screaming at me that the world would be better off without me.
Let's go somewhere warmer and talk a while. I want to help you.
Thank you all for heeding my summons.
My liege, what is this about?
Rumors. Insidious rumors are chipping away at my throne, Bernardo.
The ghost of my brother? Truly? My brother's soul is at peace, God rest him.
How did you hear of this?
Lady Ophelia told me, of course.
Ophelia? You told him?
I thought it could help.
Regardless of the spread of this rumor, what is important is that it stops.
If I hear any more of this, I will be forced to action.
This is a direct threat to me and to my rule. And I will not suffer your indignities to the extent your mother has.
My lord, it was just idle chatter. You know how gossip spreads.
'Idle' chatter? Claiming to see the spirit of my dead brother is insulting. It's macabre at best and a detriment to his name at worst.
My brother's immortal soul rests in Heaven, with the Almighty. Where he belongs.
I expect better from all of you than to speak ill of a dead man. No more wagging tongues.
Are you afraid?
Tch. Afraid! Hardly.
Your quaking hand gives you away.
Hmm. I bid you all a less imaginative evening.
How... how could you?
When you spoke to my uncle about seeing my father's ghost. It... he... threatened me.
Because of you, he now wants me dead, and all my best laid plans are useless.
Hamlet, I... I thought if I—
No. You helped me see.
I was weak. I let my feelings get in the way of my judgement. But it's all become clear to me now.
'Become clear'?
Oh! Everyone thinks I'm mad. And they're right. I am. I'm daft. I'm insane.
Time to take action at last!
You see, Ophelia, when I came to understand you of all people had betrayed me, I realized something wonderful.
None of this matters. It doesn't matter if I get revenge for my father's death. It doesn't matter if I expose my uncle.
There's nothing worth living for. Not you, not my mother, not Claudius, not any of them or any of it.
As long as I thought you were still my friend, there was some shred of purpose in living. But now? I'm free.
Hamlet. I am your friend. I don't want to bring harm to you. I was just trying to help.
You're too clever to possibly believe that.
My mind is clear for the first time in a long time. And I feel peaceful. And you won't take that from me.
Time to do now what I ought to have done months ago.
(This isn't good. He's coming undone.)
So. I'm not going to Paris after all.
I hope staying behind is worth the trouble. And that father isn't too enraged with me.
The game is Ruff and Honours, gentlemen.
What's wrong, Marcellus?
Marcellus is quite the poor loser, ja?
Close yer lips, old woman. I ain't about to lose t'yeh!
I'm jus' so bloody tired of this game, thas' all!
Deal 'em out, Horatio. Gimme somethin' good!
It's spades. Of course. Bloody hell.
Lucky play, obviously. Your trick, Marcellus.
Next—looks like spades again.
Mein Gott, Marcellus. I swear to Heaven—
He had King and Queen?
Warrrhar har har! I'm only gettin' started!
(I don't even know the rules.)
Ophelia told me you'd be here. But I didn't believe it.
G-Guard Captain!
If you have time to gamble, surely you have time to train harder. Need I remind you all that we could be at war at any moment?
This level of discipline is shameful. I won't have it in my ranks.
Laps. Now. Put the cards down and get running.
Y-yes, sir!
You can't make me run! I'm not under your command!
You've been arranging games like this for months. I know where all your earnings are kept.
If you'd like me not to confiscate those, I suggest you spend less time acting like a two-copper tavern wench and more time serving your ladyship. Now—go.
Y-you're a tyrant!
Clearly I haven't supervised them closely enough.
Where did I go wrong, Ophelia? Was it the drills?
Was I too hard on them? Are they acting out in spite? Is this merely a phase?
I gave them everything! They just don't appreciate me!
Some fresh air and exercise never hurt anyone. I'm sure they'll forgive you.
Yes, Lady Birgitta? Does something trouble you?
My lady, I have a request.
I cannot bear it any longer.
I'd like to leave Elsinore.
You want to leave the castle? For what purpose?
